## 1) Formal access governance (policy/process language)
Evidence would include emails or attachments that reference:
- **Named policies** (e.g., “access policy,” “IT security policy,” “SOX controls,” “user access review”)
- **Approval workflows** (e.g., “request access via ticket,” “manager approval required,” “Security must approve”)
- **Auditing/reviews** (e.g., “quarterly access recertification,” “access review,” “remove dormant accounts”)

## 2) Role-based access (RBAC-style language)
Evidence would include:
- References to **roles/groups** rather than ad-hoc permissions (e.g., “add user to group X,” “role-based access,” “entitlement,” “least privilege”)
- Mentions of **job-function mapping** (e.g., “trader role,” “finance role,” “system administrator role”)

- **More frequent access removals** or “deprovisioning” notices (e.g., “disable accounts,” “revoke access,” “terminate access immediately”)
- **Tighter approval requirements** (e.g., “no exceptions,” “only Security can grant,” “additional sign-off required”)
- **Shorter access windows** or “temporary access” becoming the norm
- **Escalations** when people request broader access (e.g., “denied,” “requires justification,” “not permitted under policy”)
- **Emergency controls** (e.g., “lock down,” “freeze,” “restrict admin rights,” “limit production access”)

## What to search for in your corpus (practical query terms)
If you’re doing this analysis yourself, common keywords/phrases that often surface these themes include:
- **Governance/process:** “policy,” “procedure,” “approval,” “ticket,” “change control,” “audit,” “recertification,” “SOX,” “controls”
- **Role-based:** “role,” “group,” “entitlement,” “least privilege,” “RBAC,” “access matrix,” “job function”
- **Restrictive trend:** “revoke,” “disable,” “deprovision,” “lock down,” “temporary access,” “no exceptions,” “denied,” “escalate,” “freeze”
